messages:
sophie: Heads-up: after the kernel selector patch, host-side tokenization latency spiked on small requests (~1.8ms -> 3.6ms). Perf graphs show tail increase. Anyone else seeing this?
ryan: saw it on prod canary, yes. traces point to extra memcpy in parse step.
arjun: which traces? can you paste flame sample?
sophie: dug in with flame: host preparse spends ~72% in `parse_request` memcpy + utf8 checks. Kernel selector's batch-hint is smaller, causing extra unpacking allocations.
sophie: perf snippet:
```
perf top -p 12345
parse_request+0x1a7  72.4%
tokenize_utf8+0x3b   15.1%
kv_cache_lookup+0x10 8.0%
```
ryan: also seeing grpc writev overhead increase after chunker tweak — smaller fragments -> worse coalescing.
sophie: hypothesis: batching heuristic reduced window_size -> more fragments -> more memmoves in reassembly.
ana: quick mitigation: reintroduce inline fast-path for small payloads (<128b) to avoid allocator overhead.
ana: also consider increasing coalesce threshold in grpc proxy.
ryan: i'll open a tiny PR with allocator-bypass + unit test.
sophie: can we run canary env with `HOST_PREPARSE_INLINE=1`? perf-bot: starting canary...
perf-bot: canary started on canary-3 region (id: canary-3a)
perf-bot: canary metrics: p50 decode -0.1ms, p99 -0.9ms, cpu -6% on preparse host.
ryan: looks promising. merging PR once tests pass.
sophie: i'll follow up with kv cache hit-ratio before/after and grpc small-write metrics.
arjun: add a microbenchmark for tokenization (len 8/32/128/512) to guard regressions.
sophie: added perf checklist to PR.
ryan: LGTM :thumbsup: 
perf-bot: deploy complete, canary stable for 30m.
